If you call dbDisconnect() on the failed connection does your TCP issue go away?

Neil

drv = dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
con = dbConnect(drv, host="host", port="5432", dbname="dbname",
  user="user", password="password")

I get this error in R:

Error in postgresqlNewConnection(drv, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver: (could not connect user@host on dbname "dbname"
)

I am seeing this in the logs for the PostgreSQL database:

user [MAROON] FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry for host "my ip address", 
  user "user", database "dbname", SSL off

I am not sure what that means, and what I can do about it.

Hi Eric,

(2013/03/15 11:25), Eric wrote:
> I just installed R 2.15.3 on Windows.
> I am trying to access PostgreSQL database on Heroku, and have run into an error.
>
> I installed package with Packages -> Install package(s) and selected PostgreSQL.
>
> My program looks like this, with placeholders for important information:
>
> drv = dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
> con = dbConnect(drv, host="host", port="5432", dbname="dbname",
>    user="user", password="password")
>
> I get this error in R:
>
> Error in postgresqlNewConnection(drv, ...) :
>    RS-DBI driver: (could not connect user@host on dbname "dbname"
> )
>
> I am seeing this in the logs for the PostgreSQL database:
>
> user [MAROON] FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry for host "my ip address",
>    user "user", database "dbname", SSL off
>
> I am not sure what that means, and what I can do about it.
> Is there something that I missed while installing RPostgreSQL? Thanks.

Actually, it is not about RPostgreSQL.

It means you need to modify pg_hba.conf, a config file for Host-Based 
Access Control of PostgreSQL, to allow remote connection from your 
Windows to PostgreSQL (Heroku) server.

See the PostgreSQL doc for more details about pg_hba.conf.
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.2/static/auth-pg-hba-conf.html

Regards,
--

Hi Neil,

> Why does libpq in the src/libpq folder compile for Mac OS X?

It was configured to make binaries on CRAN.
The system used in CRAN are 
macosx-x86_64 	 r-prerel 	 MacOS X 	 x86_64	 Mac OS X 10.6.8 	 MacPro, Intel Xeon 54XX @ 2.80GHz 	 GCC 4.2.1 
or
macosx-ix86 	 r-release 	 MacOS X 	 ix86	 Mac OS X 10.5.8 (9L31a) 	 MacPro, Intel Xeon 54XX @ 2.80GHz 	 GCC 4.2.1 

(http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html#r-release-macosx-ix86)
To my understanding, these system does not come with PostgreSQL preinstalled.

A more recent versions of Mac OS X may have preinstalled libpq library.
http://www.postgresql.org/download/macosx/

So, it is better to detect them if available, but I don't 
have access to such system right now.

messages.body_plain:
Tomoaki,

I would expect that if libpq is found that there would be no need to build libpq in src/libpq. So it appears that one of two problems exist.

1) When running RPostgreSQL in R, R is using libpq installed by the PostgreSQL database installation.  It unnecessarily builds libpq when installing from source even if libpq is available. No harm. No change needed as it ignores the src/libpq built version at runtime. (Further testing indicates this is not the case.)

2) RPostgreSQL uses the built version of libpq in src/libpq at runtime.  This version is older and may not be matched to the currently installed version of PostgreSQL.  Someone has to periodically update the source in src/libpq in to keep up with the database source.  Version mismatches can occur.

So then I did some testing with
	OS X 10.8.3, OS installed PostgreSQL 9.1.5, as reported by pg_config.
Change path and
	OS X 10.8.3, custom installed PostgreSQL 9.2.2 as reported by pg_config.

After compiling the source for RPostgreSQL in both cases, it appears on Mac OS X that RPostgreSQL is reporting libpq version 9.1.1 (which is the version in src/libpq).  This means RPostgreSQL is not only compiling when it does not need to, but that RPostgreSQL is not using the database installed version of libpq when it is available.  In both cases pg_config reported the correct version of postgresql and the configure test for libpq-fe.h picked up the correct version.  It does not appear that configure ever checks for libpq.

Unless I am missing something, this seems less than optimal and potentially problematic.

I have access to systems to test, but I don't have enough knowledge of how the build/runtime systems work to just go in and change it.  Is there any way I can help clean this up? I have Macs with 10.8.3, 10.7.5, 10.6.8, and 10.5.8 (ppc).  In this regard, the Mac should behave much the same as linux.  

What am I missing?  

Neil

CRAN policy states "Package authors should make all reasonable efforts to provide cross-platform portable code. Packages will not normally be accepted that do not run on at least two of the major R platforms."

return some information under non-gcc environment and work fine.
